Q: Return value from arr.reduce() method. Return last value of array, intead of object A:

arr.reduce method return the accumulator which is the first argument. So why the last value of array is return in my code.

See the documentation on MDN:

The reduce() method is an iterative method. It runs a "reducer" callback function over all elements in the array, in ascending-index order, and accumulates them into a single value. Every time, the return value of callbackFn is passed into callbackFn again on next invocation as accumulator. The final value of accumulator (which is the value returned from callbackFn on the final iteration of the array) becomes the return value of reduce().

The accumulator is passed in to the callback function as the first argument, but it is determined by the return value of the callback function.

The result of evaluating the expression obj[value.id] = value is value so in the second example you are returning value from the callback function instead of obj from the function.

Q: Android: external storage permission issue: A:

According to the documentation, the state you're describing means that the external media storage isn't accessible to you:

public static final String MEDIA_SHARED

Added in API level 1 getExternalStorageState() returns MEDIA_SHARED if the media is present not mounted, and shared via USB mass storage.

Constant Value: "shared"

You need to go to your USB Mass Storage options and turn off USB storage.

Q: Gitlab runner: verify vs status A:

gitlab-runner. exe status tells you, if the Service is running. It seems that you've stopped it with gitlab-runner.exe stop.

gitlab-runner.exe verify tells you if your Runner is still registered to a GitLab Instance. If you or someone else removed it in the GitLab CI/CD settings, your Runner wouldn't be alive anymore.

Q: Installation of graphics drivers for RTX Pro 6000 Blackwell and 24.04 environment A:

1. Install newer kernel

Install mainline kernel ≥ 6.11:

sudo apt install mainline
mainline install 6.12

Reboot into that kernel.

2. Remove all existing NVIDIA drivers

sudo apt purge 'nvidia-*'
sudo apt autoremove

3. Install latest driver from NVIDIA (not apt)

Download latest .run driver from NVIDIA website.

Then install:

sudo systemctl isolate multi-user.target
sudo bash NVIDIA-Linux-*.run

  • Enable DKMS → YES

  • Nouveau → already disabled

4. Disable GSP firmware (important)

sudo nano /etc/modprobe.d/nvidia.conf

Add:

options nvidia NVreg_EnableGpuFirmware=0

5. Set kernel parameters

Edit:

sudo nano /etc/default/grub

Change:

GRUB_CMDLINE_LINUX_DEFAULT="quiet splash"

to:

GRUB_CMDLINE_LINUX_DEFAULT="quiet splash nvidia-drm.modeset=1"

Update:

sudo update-grub

6. Disable Secure Boot

If enabled, NVIDIA modules won’t load properly.
